newsitem.title: ITALY: Arafat arrives in Italy day after summit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat arrives in Italy day after summit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Rome on Thursday for talks at the Vatican and with Italian leaders after an ice-breaking summit with Israel's new right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Arafat made no comment to reporters after his arrival at Ciampino military airport.

He was due to hold talks with senior Vatican officials and with members of the Italian government as well as meeting Rome community leaders, including top representatives of the city's ancient Jewish community.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy also arrived in Rome on Thursday for talks with his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini. Diplomats said Levy and Arafat were not expected to meet.
Arafat and Netanyahu met for the first time on Wednesday for a brief summit on the Israeli-Gazan border to relaunch stalled talks on extending Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza.

Though they did not solve major problems, the meeting and a reserved handshake were seen as vital symbols of both sides' commitment to the Oslo agreement signed with the PLO by the Labour government that Netanyahu toppled in May.
Arafat was due to fly north later on Thursday for a weekend international business forum at the lakeside Italian resort of Cernobbio.

Israel's former prime minister Shimon Peres, one of the architects of the Oslo accord and the man Netanyahu defeated in the May election, is also scheduled to take part in the Cernobbio gathering, which begins on Friday.
